answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry makes each identity costly: an agent must lock a bond and build history before it can trade, and a single quill of misbehavior slashes that bond, so spawning thousands of throwaway identities costs more than any delta in profit they could extract. The registry leaves no safe haven for cheap clones — every new identity starts at zero trust and must earn it slowly through verifiable work, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
